data.claim: A child that closes stdout shortly before exiting makes verify_one's post-EOF single waitid(WNOHANG) sample return None, so it reports 'closed its output' instead of 'exited (N)'.
data.falsifier: A child that closes stdout then sleeps then exits still yields 'exited (4)' from a single post-EOF WNOHANG sample.
data.mechanism: Python closes fd 1 during interpreter shutdown, before the process terminates; the parent's select/read wakes on pipe EOF in that window, and one WNOHANG probe misses the not-yet-visible exit. A bound that polls waitid until the exit becomes visible (or a short grace lapses) recovers the status.

data.question: Does verify_one lose a child's exit code when stdout's EOF arrives before the exit is visible to waitid?

data.summary: While fix-B297ede2447 ran ddflow_review, the localhost qwen3.8 reviewer truncated at 32000 reasoning tokens and retried ~900 s. During that load the session lost every ddflow_* MCP tool: subsequent calls answered "Model tried to call unavailable tool". A new server process appeared (ps: python -m ddflow.surfaces.mcp) but the running session tool list never regained ddflow; only a session restart would. A slow or crashing reviewer must not take the MCP server down, and the client/server should support reconnect or an explicit "server restarted" signal.
data.title: MCP server dies under a heavy reviewer call and the session never regains its tools

data.summary: On 2026-10-04 ddflow_gate_run unit_tests (534 s) and ddflow_review held the ddflow MCP server so that every other ddflow MCP call (brief, show, gate_status, heartbeat) returned "MCP error -32001: Request timed out" for the whole run. The surface is unusable during any long tool, so the agent cannot check state, heartbeat its lease, or observe progress; there is no job id to poll.
data.title: A long gate or review blocks the whole MCP server; every other call times out

data.summary: The interrupted ddflow_review for rubber_duck on fix-B297ede2447 recorded only gates.rubber_duck = {at: ...} and no outcome. Re-running started a FULL round again (no resume from the marker); an earlier ddflow_gate_run whose client timed out also never delivered its result to the caller although the server finished and recorded. Suggest: long tools return a job id immediately and are pollable, and an interrupted review either completes server-side or records unavailable with a reason.
data.title: A client timeout/disconnect loses a review and leaves a start marker with no outcome
